carbon_policy_signal.item: COP31 draft text signals weakening commitment to immediate fossil-fuel phase-out; EU methane rules delayed 2 years following US pressure campaign.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Softened fossil-fuel language and methane-compliance deferrals reduce regulatory urgency for thermal-to-renewable fuel switching; structural EUA support weakens as market reprices lower decarbonization compliance cost.

freshness_caveat: Coal (as_of 2025-12-26, 329 days old) and Clean Dark (as_of 2025-12-31, 324 days old) are stale; analyses exclude these series. All forward-looking scenarios rely on fresh TTF, DE Power, GB Power, Storage, Renewable Share, and EUA data (as_of 2026-11-19 to 2026-11-20, 0–1 days old).
risk_flags: EU storage 17.8 pp below seasonal; refill pace will anchor winter power curve and TTF forward risk.
Clean Spark 93rd percentile yet monthly change is -60.9 EUR/MWh — high volatility suggests mean reversion tail risk.
EU methane rules delayed 2 years; compliance cost pressure on gas disappears, undermining structural TTF support.
COP31 fossil-fuel language softening increases likelihood of prolonged coal/gas dispatch globally; EUA (35th percentile, -2.5σ) reflects this policy discount.

base.summary: Gas in-the-money, storage deficit sustains thermal support; policy drift eases EUA upside.

downside.summary: COP31 fossil-fuel text finalizes with weak language; methane-rule delay signals policy retreat; EUA reprices lower.

upside.summary: Sanctions escalation on Russia isolates winter gas supply; EU refill pace misses seasonal; TTF reprices tighter.

themes: Gas firmly in-the-money; storage deficit sustains thermal call
COP31 and methane-rule delay weaken long-term decarbonization urgency
Sanctions posture hardening on Russia; winter supply tail-risk rising
US LNG inventory surplus reduces winter export arbitrage
top_drivers: Clean Spark at 93rd percentile (43.91 EUR/MWh) reflects sustained gas-in-the-money thermal premium despite -60.9 EUR/MWh monthly reversion.
EU storage deficit (69.83%, 17.8 pp below seasonal) anchors winter thermal-call and TTF structural support; refill pace will drive H1 2027 risk.
COP31 fossil-fuel language and EU methane-rule 2-year delay remove medium-term decarbonization compliance cost pressure; bearish for EUA (35th percentile, extended -2.5σ) and power-curve steepness.
top_takeaway: Clean Spark at 93rd percentile signals sustained gas-in-the-money regime; EU storage 17.8 pp below seasonal average underpins structural thermal support, offset by delayed EU methane rules and COP31 fossil-fuel language softening.

watchlist.why: Outcome determines whether immediate phase-out language resurfaces; material for EUA curve and power-generation marginal cost expectations.

watchlist.metric: EU sanctions envoy mandate (Russia energy isolation)
watchlist.why: Escalation over next 2–4 weeks could reprrice winter gas supply premium; direct transmission to TTF and German/GB power forwards.
Currently 17.8 pp below seasonal; refill speed will determine whether thermal dispatch headroom persists into H1 2027.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export economics (Hormuz flows, storage surplus)
watchlist.why: Above-average US inventories + 19% Hormuz throughput surge reduce arbitrage pull to EU; indirect bearish transmission to TTF spot.
